newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields end lower after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields end lower after U.S. data.

text.p: 1550 GMT - Swedish bond yields ended lower on Tuesday, falling after U.S. labour cost data for the fourth quarter was better than expected.
The crown strengthened a little on comments by Riksbank Governor Urban Backstrom who said the crown was weaker than it should be. He also said the inflation outlook was unchanged.

The Riksbank left its key interst rate, the repo rate, unchanged at 4.10 percent at its weekly tender. * Six-month T-bill rates rise one basis point to 3.99 pct * Nine-year bond yields slip eight basis points to 6.72 pct * Crowns firms to 4.4110 to the mark from 4.4260 late Monday
Long Swedish debt yields reversed morning losses to close substantially lower and the crown firmed on Tuesday.

A better-than-expected U.S. fourth quarter employment cost index fuelled the decrease. Several players sold before Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, said it would leave its key repurchase rate at an unchanged fixed 4.10 percent.
Comments by Riksbank Governor Urban Backstrom added to the market optimism.
"Backstrom's speech was positively received. There will be more cuts but they will come later," one dealer said.

Six-month T-bill rates rose one basis point to 3.99 percent while the nine-year bond yield dropped eight basis points to 6.72 percent after rising. The spread between Swedish and German long yields decreased six basis points to 94.
Backstrom said that the current crown rate did not reflect fundamental trends in the Swedish economy. The crown firmed to 4.4110 versus the mark versus 4.4260 late on Monday.
"We trust that Backstrom will work in the direction so the crown doesn't weaken more. Foreign players as well as Swedish ones have bought crowns on that," a dealer said.
